bullets.text: Operating income rose to $212.7M ($2.76/share); net income +3% to $274.3M ($3.59/share); ROE 27.4% vs 36.0%; underwriting profit was 8.3% (11.5% including $71M supplemental reserve elimination).
NPW increased 35% to $2,457.2M ($638M increase); Core division NPW grew 38% to $2,341M (95% of company NPW); Diversified business NPW fell to $115M from $118M in 1993.
Underwriting expenses were reduced by 3.0 percentage points, following a 3.5 point reduction in 1993; expenses reached 24% of premiums, down from 26% in 1993 and 31% in 1989.
Investments grew to $3.18B; total return was 3.7% (beating benchmark by 4.3 pts); issued $200M 10-year notes; repurchased 1,080,300 common shares at $31.44 average cost.
Repositioning to insure all auto risks, expanding from nonstandard auto into the $80B standard and preferred market, and seeking to be continuously less involved in non-auto commercial insurance.
Independent agents accounted for over 90% of 1994 volume among 30,000+ participating agents; consumers offered buying choices via agents, telephone, mail, or direct Progressive locations.

Promoted 1-800-AUTO-PRO Express Quote via TV and direct mail, providing competitor rate comparisons; brand offering was sold throughout Florida, in Texas, and in Ohio, with 24/7 immediate claims response.
Targets a 4% underwriting profit margin in each program; offers prices to every licensed driver, allowing volume from the newly served market to grow to 5% to 10% of 1994 volume.

Progressive is the 7th largest U.S. private passenger auto insurer with 2.2% market share, surpassed only by State Farm, Allstate, Farmers, USAA, Nationwide, and GEICO, and compares itself to them and Safeco.
Gainsharing links compensation to cost reduction, profit, and growth; recognized by Fortune for management re-engineering; consolidated Cleveland staff into a new 517,800 square foot headquarters.
